intro: Considered preparation. Beautiful finishes. Color that belongs in the rooms you call home.
serviceTitle: A considered finish for every space.

story.title: The finish begins underneath.
story.text: A beautiful result depends on the surface you start with. Preparation, protection, product selection, and drying time belong in the plan—not in the fine print.
points: Sample color in the actual light
Plan how the home stays usable

guide.title: Good work, layer by layer.
guide.intro: A painting brief should make the invisible work as clear as the final color.

notes.title: Look closely
notes.text: Identify peeling, cracks, moisture concerns, and existing coatings. Older buildings may need specialist assessment before disturbing painted surfaces.

notes.title: Prepare thoughtfully
notes.text: Agree protection, cleaning, repair, sanding, and priming appropriate to the surface. The proposal should explain what preparation is included.

notes.title: Choose in context
notes.text: Test samples in the space and observe them in changing light. Discuss sheen, durability, and the manufacturer’s care recommendations.

notes.title: Plan the handover
notes.text: Allow for access, ventilation, drying, and curing according to the selected products. Record colors and finishes for future touch-ups.

faq.q: Can you help narrow down colors?
faq.a: A real color consultation can consider light, adjoining finishes, and sample boards. The showroom color picker changes this website, not the walls in the stock photographs.

faq.q: Does every room need the same finish?
faq.a: No. Surface condition, use, light, and product requirements influence the choice. The estimate brief collects your preferences for discussion.

faq.q: Are the photos your completed projects?
faq.a: No. They are illustrative stock images selected to show interiors and painting craft, not a portfolio of this fictional business.
